deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the opening (draft) page of Riemann's 1857 memoir 'Zwei allgemeine Sätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten'. The draft title reads 'Theoreme'. Dedekind and Weber published it in the Werke (1876) from the Nachlass. The page contains no computations. It is a motivating reduction followed by definitions.

(1) Reduction to the monodromy setting. Consider a homogeneous linear ODE L(y) = y^(n) + p_1(x) y^(n-1) + ... + p_n(x) y = 0. It is 'well known' that every solution is a constant-coefficient linear combination y = sum c_i y_i of n independent particular solutions y_1..y_n.
- Rational coefficients p_k(x): the solution is in general a many-valued function. Each branch is expressible linearly in functions that are completely determined (locally single-valued) for every x.
- Algebraic coefficients: each p_k is rational in x and in one many-valued algebraic function s(x), i.e. p_k = R_k(x, s). To each branch of s there belongs a system of n independent particular solutions.
- So every branch of a solution is again a constant-coefficient linear expression in completely determined functions. That expression goes over into one of the same kind when x circles a singular or branch value.
- Hence the theorems to follow, stated for systems of functions with linear monodromy, cover all linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients.

(2) Object of study (begun here, restated cleanly on folio 22v). Consider functions y_1..y_n of x that are single-valued ('einändrig') and finite for all complex x except a, b, ..., t. Under a closed circuit of x around one of these values they go over into linear functions of themselves with constant coefficients: y -> A y.

(3) Orientation convention. A circuit is positive when the boundary of a region containing the branch value is traversed so that the inward direction relates to the direction of motion as +i relates to 1. In other words the interior lies to the left, i.e. counterclockwise. My check: for x = a + r e^{it} the tangent is i r e^{it} and the inward normal is -e^{it} = i·(i e^{it}).

(4) Definition of 'einändrig' (Cauchy's 'monodrome'). A function of one or several variables is einändrig near a value or value-system if [garbled draft: roughly, it takes one determinate, continuously varying value at all neighbouring points]. By a known theorem (Cauchy), einändrig is equivalent to expandability in positive integer powers of the increments of the variables, i.e. holomorphy.

(5) Branch values. A branch value is a value at which one branch of a function continues into another.
- For one variable it is a single point.
- For several variables it is given by an equation among the variables (a hypersurface).
- Example: a is a branch value of (x-a)^mu when mu is not an integer. Draw any line from a. The function can be fixed near a so that it varies continuously off the line, but it takes different values on the two sides. Continuing across the line produces a different branch: (x-a)^mu is multiplied by e^{2 pi i mu} per positive circuit.
- Conversely, a is not a branch value if the function is expandable in integer powers of x-a. Here 'ganze Potenzen' presumably means a Laurent-type expansion, so poles are permitted.
errors: No mathematical errors. The page is a heavily corrected draft whose definitions are sometimes stated imprecisely.

Equating 'einändrig' with power-series expandability implicitly requires finiteness/analyticity (single-valued and monogenic, bounded near the point). As written in the draft, single-valuedness alone would not suffice.

The criterion 'not a branch value if expandable in integer powers of x-a' is sufficient but phrased loosely. Single-valuedness around a is what matters; poles or essential singularities do not create branching.
The sentence on algebraic coefficients is syntactically broken in the draft. The intended claim (one fundamental system per branch of the algebraic irrationality) is correct.

results.what: Every solution of a homogeneous linear ODE of order n is a constant-coefficient combination of n independent solutions
results.modern_name: Fundamental system of solutions / n-dimensional solution space

results.what: Reduction of linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients to systems of functions with branch points whose circuits act by constant linear substitutions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (this memoir, Werke 1876); Fuchs 1865-66 for the ODE side

results.what: Definition of 'einändrig' (Cauchy's monodrome) and its equivalence with power-series expandability
Branch point definition with cut-line description; (x-a)^mu example; positive orientation convention (interior as +i to 1)
results.modern_name: Branch point, branch cut, counterclockwise orientation

results.what: Branch locus for several variables is given by an equation among the variables

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft introduction of Riemann's well-known 1857 monodromy memoir, published in his Werke (1876). The content is known to be his. Minor draft details (the title 'Theoreme', the explicit several-variables remark) are only of philological interest.

checkable.asserts: For counterclockwise traversal the inward normal equals i times the unit tangent, so 'interior as +i to 1' means positive = counterclockwise (result 0).
One positive circuit around a multiplies (x-a)^mu by exp(2*pi*I*mu), which differs from 1 iff mu is not an integer.
(x-a)^mu solves the first-order linear ODE (x-a)y' - mu*y = 0 with rational coefficients, illustrating a solution with a branch point at a (result 0).
Trivial consistency placeholder; the substantive monodromy check is the exp(2*pi*I*mu) factor above.

transcription_corrections: Title in the image reads 'Zwei allgemeine Theoreme über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten'. The published version reads 'Sätze'.
'welche sie genügt' should probably read 'welcher sie genügt' (the ODE which it satisfies).
'die von Begrenzung [...] in einer Richtung durchläuft' is better read as '(dessen) Begrenzung ... in einer Richtung durchläuft': the boundary of the region containing the branch value.

In the einändrig definition the phrase 'in der Nachbarschaft' and the following clause are heavily struck/garbled. The surviving sense is 'wenn allen Werthen oder Werthencombinationen ... ein bestimmter Werth entspricht'.
Marginal folio number '22' visible at right. The interlinear insertion above line 1 reads 'n von einander unabhängigen' and refers to the particular solutions.
'durch eine Gleichung zwischen den W.[erthen] der veränderlichen Grössen gebildet': the abbreviation W. = Werthen.
